name: Syndrome Associated with Dilated Cardiomyopathy

criteria.description: Echocardiographic evidence of left ventricular dilatation
Left ventricular ejection fraction less than 45%
Exclusion of ischemic, valvular, hypertensive, or congenital heart disease
Family history of dilated cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death
Identification of pathogenic mutation in cardiomyopathy-associated genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of left ventricular dilatation and reduced ejection fraction with exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and family history support diagnosis but are not mandatory

common.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output
chest pain not from heart attack

occasional.symptomName: Ascites due to right heart failure
searchTerms: ascites due to right heart issues

rare.symptomName: Thromboembolic events secondary to ventricular dysfunction
searchTerms: blood clots from weak heart pumping
clot formation due to poor heart function
liver swelling due to heart failure

rare.symptomName: Neurological symptoms due to cerebral embolism

laboratory: Elevated B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP
Mild elevation of liver enzymes in congestive hepatopathy
imaging: Echocardiography showing left ventricular dilatation and reduced ejection fraction
Cardiac MRI demonstrating myocardial fibrosis and ventricular enlargement
genetic: Pathogenic mutations in genes such as TTN, LMNA, MYH7
other: Electrocardiogram abnormalities including conduction delays and arrhythmias
Endomyocardial biopsy may show nonspecific myocardial fibrosis

distinguishingFeatures: Regional wall motion abnormalities on imaging
Presence of coronary artery stenosis on angiography

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe heart failure symptoms
Ventricular arrhythmias or sudden cardiac arrest
Rapid progression of left ventricular dysfunction
references: Maron BJ, Towbin JA, Thiene G, et al. Contemporary definitions and classification of the cardiomyopathies: an American Heart Association Scientific Statement. Circulation. 2006;113(14):1807-1816.
Orphanet: Syndrome associated with dilated cardiomyopathy - ORPHA:217619

Elliott P, Andersson B, Arbustini E, et al. Classification of the cardiomyopathies: a position statement from the European Society Of Cardiology Working Group on Myocardial and Pericardial Diseases. Eur Heart J. 2008;29(2):270-276.
